text: Observe the month of Abib and keep the Passover to the LORD your God, for it was in the month of Abib that the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
You shall sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God from the flock and the herd, at the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for his name.

You shall eat no leavened bread with it. For seven days you shall eat with it unleavened bread, the bread of affliction—for you came out of the land of Egypt in haste—so that all the days of your life you may remember the day you left the land of Egypt.

versions.text: You shall eat no leavened bread with it. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction—for you came out of the land of Egypt in haste—so that all the days of your life you may remember the day you left the land of Egypt.
versions.explanation: The repetition of "with it" at the end of two consecutive clauses stumbles when read aloud; shifting the phrase forward in the second clause smooths the rhythm without losing the Hebrew's repeated עָלָיו.

text: No leaven shall be found anywhere in your territory for seven days, and none of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day shall remain until morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of your towns that the LORD your God is giving you.
Only at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name shall you sacrifice the Passover, in the evening at sunset, the appointed time when you came out of Egypt.

versions.text: Only at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name shall you sacrifice the Passover, in the evening at sunset, the hour you came out of Egypt.
versions.explanation: מוֹעֵד means "appointed time/season," not a specific "hour"; since verse 1 says the exodus happened by night, "the hour" at sunset creates an unnecessary tension. "The appointed time" is both more accurate and clear when read aloud.

text: Cook it and eat it at the place the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you may turn back and go to your tents.
For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God; you shall do no work.
Count off seven weeks; begin to count the seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
Then keep the Feast of Weeks to the LORD your God with a freewill offering in proportion to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.

And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite in your towns, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow among you—at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and be careful to keep these statutes.
Keep the Feast of Booths for seven days, after you have gathered in the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress.
Rejoice at your feast—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who live in your towns.

For seven days you shall celebrate the feast to the LORD your God at the place the LORD will choose, for the LORD your God will bless you in all your harvest and in all the work of your hands, and your joy will be complete.

Three times a year all your men shall appear before the LORD your God at the place he will choose: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Booths. And no one shall appear before the LORD empty-handed.
Each shall give as he is able, in proportion to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
Appoint judges and officials for yourselves in all the towns the LORD your God is giving you, tribe by tribe, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
Do not pervert justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
Justice, and justice alone, you shall pursue, so that you may live and take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving you.
Do not plant any tree as a sacred pole beside the altar you build for the LORD your God,
and do not set up a sacred pillar, for such things the LORD your God hates.

versions.text: and do not set up a sacred pillar, for the LORD your God hates them.
versions.explanation: The plural pronoun "them" has no clear singular antecedent ("a sacred pillar"); rendering the relative clause as "such things the LORD your God hates" preserves the Hebrew relative construction and reads cleanly aloud.
